title: Etale locally closed exceptional restriction and finite quotient coefficients
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and integers $n\ge m\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$, $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^m)$ with the quotient map. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $g:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion, $j:S\hookrightarrow Z$ open, and $s=gj$. Work exclusively on small etale sites, with constant coefficient rings and ordinary unbounded module derived categories. Set $Rs_{!,A}=g_{*,A}j_!$, $Rs_A^!=j^*Rg_A^!$, where $g_*\dashv Rg^!$ is the ordinary etale closed exceptional adjunction, and similarly over $B$. Let $F_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ on each scheme $T$; let $D^b_{ctf}$ mean bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, tested against all degree-zero module sheaves.

For $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, put $N_g=Rg_A^!M$. Both $N_g$ and $j^*N_g$ are finite-Tor bounded constructible. Let $c_{g,N} : F_Xg_{*,A}N\xrightarrow{\sim}g_{*,B}F_ZN$ be the canonical direct-image coefficient comparison, adjoint to coefficient change of the ordinary inverse-image/direct-image counit. The map
$$b_{g,M}:F_ZN_g\longrightarrow Rg_B^!F_XM$$
adjoint under $g_{*,B}\dashv Rg_B^!$ to $F_X(\epsilon_{g,A,M})\circ c_{g,N_g}^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. Put $b_{s,M}=j^*b_{g,M}$ after restriction/scalar identification. For $P\in D^b_{ctf}(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, let
$$q_{s,P}=g_{*,B}(q_{j,P})\circ c_{g,j_!P}:F_XRs_{!,A}P\xrightarrow{\sim}Rs_{!,B}F_SP,$$
where $q_j$ is the open extension/scalar isomorphism restricting to the identity. Then $b_{s,M}$ and $q_{s,P}$ are natural isomorphisms, $Rs_{!,A}\dashv Rs_A^!$ has counit $\epsilon_{s,A}=\epsilon_{g,A}\circ g_{*,A}(\epsilon_{j,A})$, and
$$\epsilon_{s,B,F_XM}\circ Rs_{!,B}(b_{s,M})\circ q_{s,Rs_A^!M}=F_X(\epsilon_{s,A,M}).$$
For $S=Z$ this specializes to the closed case. No pro-etale exceptional adjoint is used.

Notation and categorical conventions are those of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], [def-kun-tor-amplitude], [lem-exc-closed-ambient], [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor].

proof.text: Convert the recorded finite-value bounded-constructible and finite-Tor predicates to the source library predicates using the landed constructibility comparison, then transport finite-Tor intervals across restriction and extension by zero. The exact source interfaces are Scheme.isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff_isConstructibleSheaf, constructibleFiniteTor_leftDerivedUpperStar and constructibleTorAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory_openImmersionLowerShriek; min/max bounds handle the zero complex and initially unordered intervals.

For the finite coefficient quotient, the characteristic prime is a unit in the coefficient ring by the DVR extension-integers theorem. Hence the quotient has invertible exponent. Apply the source stability theorem for the ordinary etale right exceptional adjoint, and identify that right adjoint with the ambient closed exceptional adjoint by uniqueness of right adjoints. This gives bounded constructible finite-Tor preservation for the closed exceptional object. The ordinary etale source interface is constructibleFiniteTor_rightDerivedUpperShriek in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.Derived.Stability.UpperShriek, derived there from exists_shift_constructibleTorAmplitudeIn_rightDerivedUpperShriek (the ordinary declaration in sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation.lean_audit.slopmaster2). The current pro-etale localizing theorem attached to that node is not used. No invocation of closedImmersion_rightAdjoint_amplitude is needed.

Use the finite direct-image coefficient comparison and its naturality to define the closed coefficient map by adjunction. The inverse cancellation calculation proves its counit equation and naturality on the finite-Tor domain.

For the complementary open, use the ordinary closed-support distinguished triangle over both coefficient rings. Exact scalar extension maps the triangle; the identity on the middle term and the open comparison on the third term give a triangle morphism whose first component is an isomorphism. Full faithfulness of closed direct image and the adjunction transpose identify this component with the closed coefficient map, proving that map is an isomorphism.

Restrict the closed coefficient map and compose with the canonical open scalar restriction comparison. Naturality of the open comparison and of the closed map gives local coefficient naturality. The open counit identity together with the closed counit equation gives the locally closed counit identity.

Apply these preservation, isomorphism, naturality and counit results to the finite-Tor constructible predicate supplied in the theorem statement. The compact-support comparison is the direct-image comparison followed by the open scalar extension map, so its naturality and isomorphism follow from the same two declarations. The pasted adjunction counit is the standard counit of the composite adjunction.

lean.note: Ordinary unbounded small-etale constant-module categories only. Canonical closed coefficient map is the exceptional adjunction transpose of the inverse of the recorded direct-image comparison followed by scalar extension of its counit. The inverse is extended by zero outside its isomorphism locus; the theorem explicitly asserts its invertibility on every input used. The full comparison predicate spells out the two finite-Tor constructibility assertions, the isomorphism assertions, naturality and the pasted counit equation. The added landed dependencies supply the existing quotient map between arbitrary coefficient stages and the already published ordinary-etale finite-Tor constructible predicate. No second D^b_ctf definition is made.
